Thanks — here are the concrete test-harness details I’ll run unless you push back. These are written to minimize variance and be reproducible.

Test harness and metric definitions:
- Environment: Redwood sandbox (dedicated), GPU-backed instances similar to our production endpoint configs.
- Models: embeddings-v1 (dense FP16) and reranker-v2 (quantized INT8 variant tested too).
- Input sizes: embeddings — mean token length 12 (search queries), reranker — pairwise inputs avg 60 tokens (query + doc excerpt).
- Concurrency matrix: [1, 4, 8, 16, 32] parallel clients (sustained for 10-minute windows).
- Batch sizes: embeddings: 1/4/8; reranker: 1/2 depending on endpoint support.
- Warmup: 5-minute warmup window prior to each sustained window to populate caches and JITs.

Metrics captured per-request: start_timestamp, first_token_timestamp, last_token_timestamp, tokens_out, model_variant, cpu/gpu utilization, p95 memory, error flags. From those we compute:
- p50/p95 latency = last_token_timestamp - start_timestamp
- TTFT = first_token_timestamp - start_timestamp
- Throughput = total tokens_out / sustained_window_seconds (and qps)
- Stability = error rate (timeouts/5xx) + CPU/GPU saturation trends

Acceptance criteria (proposal):
- Reranker: p95 < 200ms @ concurrency 8; error rate < 0.5% during sustained windows.
- Embeddings: p50 < 30ms @ concurrency 8; p95 < 120ms.
- TTFT: <= 15ms for embeddings, <= 40ms for reranker (these are conservative; we can tighten if your team requires).

I’ll attach the raw logs and a summarized CSV. I’ll also run a quick quantized reranker pass to show cost-vs-latency tradeoffs.

Attachment: load_test-20260502.log (log, 120KB)

—Rishi
